@graph.name: Hashnode design system reference
@graph.headline: Hashnode design system | Refero Styles
@graph.description: Explore Hashnode's light Dev Tools design system: Blueprint Blue #1d52de, Ink Black #16191c colors, suisseIntl, Suisse Int'l typography, and DESIGN.md for...

dos: Use #1d52de for exactly one primary CTA per viewport — never two filled blue buttons competing for attention.
Set all card and button radii to 10px, hero panels to 18px, and feed cards to 14px — these three values are the entire radius vocabulary.
Apply 'ss01', 'calt', 'kern', 'liga' font features on every Suisse Intl instance — disabling ss01 visibly changes the typeface's character.
Use hairline 1px #d1d4d9 borders for separation; never reach for a drop shadow when a border does the job.
Keep body text at 16px with 1.5 line-height and headings at 18/20/30px — do not invent intermediate sizes between the 20 and 30 steps.
Limit Slate (#7b8187) to metadata, timestamps, and vote counts — never use it for body copy or headings.
Match icon color to its adjacent text color (Ink for primary, Slate for secondary) — icons are never an independent color.
donts: Do not introduce a second accent color — the entire system speaks with one blue voice.
Do not add drop shadows to cards, buttons, or panels — the inset 1px border (oklab 0 0 0 / 0.1) is the only shadow permitted.
Do not use white (#ffffff) as a surface — Canvas is #f9fafb, which gives the interface a paper-like warmth.
Do not set body text below 14px or above 18px — the 16px body with 14px secondary is the readable core.
Do not use weight 700 for body or subheadings — reserve 700 for the 30px display headline only.
Do not use Pill (9999px) radius on anything — the system is rounded-rect, not pill-shaped.
Do not place gradient fills on cards, buttons, or hero backgrounds — color is flat throughout.

colors.name: Ink Black

colors.name: Carbon

colors.name: Fog

colors.name: Paper
colors.role: Subtle surface tint behind nested elements, hover states, and tag/chip backgrounds

colors.name: Stone
colors.role: Mid-surface layer for inset panels and elevated cards between Paper and Fog

colors.name: Canvas

colors.name: Mint
colors.role: Green supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis

designSystem.layout: Persistent two-column shell: a 240–280px fixed left sidebar containing logo, primary nav, author profile, and announcement blocks, paired with a fluid main content column. The main column is a max-width 1200px centered feed that begins with a full-width hero panel (18px radius, two-column internal split: text left, illustration right), then a 'NEW & POPULAR' section header, then a two-column responsive grid of blog post cards. Section gaps are 48px; element gaps within cards are 8px. The sidebar uses a Stone (#e6e8eb) tint or Canvas with a 1px right border. Navigation is sidebar-based, not top-bar — a deliberate editorial choice that signals 'this is a reading environment, not a dashboard.'
designSystem.imagery: Imagery is editorial and restrained. The hero features a single flat illustration (hands at a typewriter on a mustard-and-mint palette) that carries all the visual warmth of the page — no photographs, no gradients, no decorative noise. Post card thumbnails are 4:3 or 1:1 crops of content imagery (screenshots, book covers, diagrams) with 8–10px radius and a 1px Fog border. No lifestyle photography, no team shots, no abstract gradient backgrounds. The visual rule: if the image is a post thumbnail, it must look like editorial content, not decoration.

similar.why: Same editorial-feed layout with a left sidebar and two-column card grid, though Dev.to leans more colorful in its accents
Same calm reading-first aesthetic, similar hairline-border card treatment, and restrained use of a single brand color for CTAs
Same monochrome newsroom palette with a single accent, same trust-in-typography-over-decoration philosophy
Same flat-surface, hairline-border, single-accent approach — though Vercel pairs it with a darker theme
Same commitment to one strong blue accent against an achromatic system, same tight type tracking and rounded-rect components

designSystem.northStar: Editorial newsroom on a gray runway — a clean monochrome feed where one electric blue accent carries all the energy.

components.name: Primary CTA Button
components.role: The sole filled action in the system
components.description: Background #1d52de, white text, 10px radius, 8px 16px padding, Suisse Intl weight 600 at 14px. No border, no shadow. Hovers shift to a slightly darker blue (approx #1741b0). Used at most once per viewport — this button must feel like a deliberate action, not a default decoration.

components.name: Blog Post Card
components.role: Feed item in the two-column post grid
components.description: Canvas (#f9fafb) background, 1px #d1d4d9 border, 14px radius, 16px padding. No shadow, no hover lift — only a subtle background tint on hover.

components.name: Hero Panel
components.role: Large welcome area at the top of the feed
components.description: Full-width inside main column, 18px radius, 1px #d1d4d9 border, Canvas background. Two-column inner layout: left text block (30px weight 700 headline with -0.75px tracking, 16px body in Slate, single blue CTA), right illustration area. No background gradient — the illustration is the color.

components.name: Vote / Comment Chip
components.role: Inline interaction count on post cards
components.description: No background, 12px Slate text with a small leading icon at 12px. 4px gap between icon and number. Optional hover: text shifts to #16191c.

components.name: Category Tag / Badge

components.name: Author Avatar + Name Row
components.description: 32px circular avatar (or 4px fallback initial square with Fog border), 8px gap, then author name at 12px weight 500 #16191c followed by '·' separator and timestamp in Slate. Tightly horizontal — no wrapping.

typography.role: suisseIntl — detected in extracted data but not described by AI

Sole text family for everything: body, headings, nav, buttons, links. Tight -0.025em tracking on larger sizes creates a confident editorial feel; the 0.05em and 0.10em tracking on smaller sizes mark small caps and category labels. Weight 500–600 is the workhorse range; 700 is reserved for the largest hero headline (30px). The 'ss01' stylistic set is active and shapes the typeface's distinctive flavor — a designer should never opt out of it.
typography.substitute: Inter (close), General Sans, or DM Sans
typography.letterSpacing: -0.025em at 30px; normal at body sizes; 0.05em–0.10em for uppercase labels

typography.role: Icon system — Jelly for soft-filled illustrated icons, Pro for sharp utility icons. Icons align to text-baseline and inherit color from the surrounding text level (Ink for primary, Slate for secondary).
typography.substitute: Lucide or Phosphor for similar outlined density

typography.role: Tiny uppercase monospace for micro-labels and badge pills where monospaced character spacing signals 'system/metadata' — extremely rare, used as a typographic accent only
typography.substitute: JetBrains Mono Bold or IBM Plex Mono SemiBold at 10px

typography.role: Font Awesome 7 Pro — detected in extracted data but not described by AI

designSystem.description: Hashnode presents an editorial newsroom aesthetic: a near-monochrome canvas of warm-cool grays where the only chromatic element is a single electric blueprint blue that does all the talking. Typography is uniformly Suisse Intl, a humanist grotesque with tight negative tracking, giving headlines a confident, typeset-in-a-publication feel rather than a dashboard utilitarian one. Surfaces are flat with hairline borders instead of shadows — the interface trusts typography and whitespace to create hierarchy, not elevation. Components feel like cards laid out on a magazine spread: rounded but not pillowy, compact but breathable, with a two-column card grid that reads like a homepage feed. Color appears sparingly as functional punctuation — links, a single CTA fill, badges — never as decoration.
designSystem.elevationPhilosophy: The system deliberately avoids drop shadows in favor of 1px hairline borders in Fog (#d1d4d9) for all component separation. The only shadow permitted is an inset 1px stroke (oklab(0 0 0 / 0.1) 0 0 0 1px inset) for inputs that need a subtle pressed-in feel. This keeps every card, button, and panel reading as flat type on flat paper — the interface trusts typography and whitespace, not depth, to establish hierarchy.
